items.title: Cascadu interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019
items.q: We were doing a concert with T.K. Blue called Motherland Connections, right?

ctx.x: I guess you can really speak to that.

Yeah and this is what, I mean, this is how I interact in the music you know. I remember doing a concert recently and I hadn’t brought out my conch horns in a long time. And I decided just to work with it and something just told me just to work with it. We were doing a concert with T.K. Blue called Motherland Connections, right? And when it came time for the solo, instead of doing a conga solo I just knew, something just guided, pick up the conch horn. And I did a solo on the conch horn. And that horn I remember…

picked up, they got their chops on the street. They got their chops on the stage. They got their chops, you know, on the road you know? And it became something that they lived. It became something that gave them — that fed their spirit. Their body might have deteriorated but their spirit and their soul was being fed by something that we can’t put our finger on.
